findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses mutable booleans and a status string to represent a workflow lifecycle instead of an enum-based typestate machine. The struct permits illegal state combinations like (status="sent", is_sent=false) or (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) with no enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can set is_sent=true while leaving status as "pending", or set both booleans inconsistently, creating states that the domain considers impossible. mark_sent mutates struct fields directly with zero validation, so callers can invoke it on an unvalidated shard and silently create an invalid workflow.
findings.fix: Replace the struct fields with an enum typestate such as `enum ShardState { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 } }` and make mark_sent a function on the source variant that returns the next variant (e.g. `impl ShardState { fn transition_to_sent(self) -> ShardState }`).

findings.problem: status field is `String`, allowing arbitrary values like "foo", "SENT", "sent", "pending" with no domain enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set status to any string at any time, bypassing intended transitions. String comparison for state decisions is fragile and allows typos or encoding variants that silently create unexpected behavior.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with an enum `pub status: ShardStatus` where `ShardStatus` has exactly the domain states (e.g. `New`, `Validated`, `Sent`). Remove the redundant `is_sent` bool once status is an enum.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are bare bools that encode lifecycle phases. With four lifecycle-relevant fields (status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) there are 2^2 * N possible bool+string combinations but only a few are valid.
findings.failure_mode: The compiler cannot prevent callers from constructing e.g. is_validated=false, is_sent=true, status="sent", or is_validated=true, is_sent=false, status="pending". Any guard function checking "is this sent?" must manually combine multiple fields, and every new boolean field doubles the state space.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single enum typestate. The `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` data moves into the variant that owns it (e.g. `ShardState::Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 }`). This makes illegal states unrepresentable at compile time.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is `Option<u64>` stored as a separate field alongside booleans that also track sent-ness. This allows the inconsistent state: is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or is_sent=false but sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123).
findings.failure_mode: A consumer checking `if item.is_sent { let t = item.sent_at_epoch_ms.unwrap(); }` will panic because the Option is None. Or a consumer checking `if item.sent_at_epoch_ms.is_some()` assumes sent but finds is_sent=false.
findings.fix: Embed `sent_at_ms: u64` directly in the enum variant: `ShardState::Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 }`. The Option disappears because only the Sent variant exists, and the value is always Some by construction.

findings.problem: id is `String`, a raw primitive that carries no domain invariants. Any string including empty, whitespace-only, or invalid byte sequences is accepted as a shard identifier.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create a ShardWorkflow with id="", id="   ", or id containing control characters. Equality comparisons on IDs may produce unexpected matches. No domain rule is enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `struct ShardId(String)` or `struct ShardId(Vec<u8>)` with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and returns a typed error. Use `ShardId` in the domain struct.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates internal state without any parse boundary or validation. It accepts a raw ShardWorkflow with arbitrary field values and silently mutates status and is_sent to "sent"/true. There is no check that the shard was validated first, no smart constructor, and no typed error return.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can take any ShardWorkflow—regardless of its is_validated, status, or sent_at_epoch_ms values—and produce a new struct that claims it is sent. This breaks the domain invariant that only validated shards may become sent, and the mutable self parameter lets callers mutate in place without any guard.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a method on the source typestate variant that returns the next variant via a typestate transition, e.g. `impl ShardState { fn transition_to_sent(self, now_ms: u64) -> Result<ShardState, TransitionError> }`. Move the function out of the imperative shell boundary into the shell layer where it coordinates validation checks before calling the pure transition.
